hero.headline: President Trump to appear on Meet the Press as midterm pressures mount
hero.teaser: Trump faces an interview Sunday following a week marked by low approval ratings and public tensions with Senate Republicans.
hero.body:
President Trump will sit down for an interview Sunday on NBC's Meet the Press after a turbulent week that saw new lows in his approval ratings and growing tensions with Senate Republicans. The conflicts with members of his own party have increasingly spilled into public view.

The interview comes as midterm elections approach and the president faces mounting political pressure on key issues including the economy. Trump's relationship with Senate Republicans has become strained as lawmakers navigate their own electoral concerns while managing their ties to the White House.

The timing of the appearance reflects broader challenges facing the administration. As the midterm campaign intensifies, the president is working to address concerns among party members about the direction of his presidency and its impact on their own electoral prospects.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration has announced several initiatives aimed at reshaping American institutions and policy. The treasury department revealed that Trump's signature will appear on US paper currency, marking the first time a sitting president's name has been featured on legal tender. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the move aligns with efforts to promote economic growth and dollar strength. The first new currency bearing Trump's signature and Bessent's will be printed in June, with additional denominations following in subsequent months.

The administration has also pursued commemorative coins featuring Trump's image. The federal arts commission approved designs for 24-carat gold coins bearing the president's likeness, a decision that comes despite federal law restricting living presidents from appearing on currency.

These efforts represent an expansion of Trump's efforts to place his name and likeness on American institutions. The administration has renamed the US Institute of Peace, the Kennedy Center performing arts venue, and commissioned a new class of battleships, among other changes.

On the international front, the administration faces challenges abroad. Tensions with Iran have escalated following a series of military exchanges between the countries, threatening the fragile ceasefire in place. The United Nations has warned that the ongoing Middle East conflict is pushing millions into hunger, with oil price increases devastating global food security. The World Food Programme director noted that negative predictions about the humanitarian situation are materializing nearly three months into the conflict.

Trade policy remains another significant challenge. The administration's approach to tariffs and trade disputes continues to generate friction with international partners and concerns about the direction of US economic policy. Analysts warn that the scattershot approach to tariffs and trade negotiations could lead to a prolonged trade war with significant global implications.

As Trump prepares for his Sunday television appearance, these interconnected pressures from within his party, economic concerns, and international challenges will likely feature prominently in the discussion.

cards.headline: US proposes using frozen Iranian assets to repair Gulf states damaged in attacks
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department plans to make Iranian assets available to US allies in the Gulf region to cover damage from Iranian strikes.
cards.body:
The US Treasury Department is preparing to use frozen Iranian assets to help Gulf allies recover from damage caused by Iranian attacks, according to a government source. The proposal would redirect confiscated funds to countries in the Gulf region that suffered infrastructure damage from Iranian military operations.

The plan represents a shift in how the US handles seized Iranian assets and aims to compensate American allies without using US taxpayer funds. Gulf states have faced repeated attacks attributed to Iran or its proxies in recent years. The Treasury Department has not announced a timeline for implementing the proposal or specified which countries would receive assistance.

cards.headline: At least 12 people shot near street festival in Toledo, Ohio
cards.body:
At least 12 people were wounded in a shooting near the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday. Two of the victims were in critical condition, according to Toledo deputy police chief Joe Heffernan.

Police believe the incident involved at least two people firing weapons at each other. Authorities have not yet apprehended any suspects and continue searching for those responsible.

The shooting occurred on the 600 block near the festival venue in this historic neighborhood known for its Victorian-era homes. Emergency responders transported the wounded to nearby hospitals. Police secured the scene and launched an active investigation to locate the suspects involved.

Heffernan described the level of violence as extraordinary for the area. The incident represents one of the larger shooting events in Toledo in recent months, with a dozen victims injured in a single occurrence marking a significant public safety concern for the community.

The Old West End Festival brings together thousands of people from the area for community celebration and cultural events. The shooting has raised broader questions about safety at public gatherings, a concern that has grown across the country in recent years.

While mass shootings at community events have prompted many cities to implement increased security measures, this particular incident appears to have stemmed from a targeted confrontation between individuals rather than a planned attack on festival attendees. The circumstances that sparked the exchange of gunfire remain under investigation.

Police have not yet released the identities of the victims or detailed information about what led to the shooting. The investigation remains active as law enforcement works to identify and apprehend the suspects responsible for the violence.

The shooting adds to growing concerns about public safety at community events nationwide. Festivals and outdoor gatherings have become focal points for security discussions among city officials and organizers. The incident in Toledo underscores the unpredictable nature of gun violence and the challenges law enforcement faces in protecting large gatherings of people.

Residents and officials in Toledo are waiting for updates as the investigation progresses. The case highlights ongoing debates about gun violence in American communities and the measures needed to keep people safe during public celebrations.

Anyone with information about the shooting has been encouraged to contact Toledo police. The department continues its search for the suspects and is asking the public for assistance in solving the case.

cards.headline: China's Xi Jinping to visit North Korea for talks with Kim Jong Un
cards.teaser: The Chinese president will make a rare trip to North Korea, arriving one day after Pyongyang reaffirmed its nuclear status and rejected US denuclearization efforts.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit North Korea next week, marking his first trip to the country since 2019. Both nations announced the visit on Friday, one day after North Korea unveiled a new facility for producing nuclear fuel.

The trip underscores Beijing's continued diplomatic engagement with Pyongyang amid ongoing tensions over the country's weapons programs. Xi's meetings with leader Kim Jong Un are expected to address bilateral relations and regional security concerns. North Korea has dismissed U.S. efforts to achieve denuclearization as "anachronistic dreams," signaling its resistance to Washington's diplomatic pressure.

cards.headline: Trump Considers Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The administration is exploring a plan for the U.S. government to take equity positions in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump is exploring the possibility of the U.S. government acquiring equity stakes in AI companies. Trump framed the proposal as a way for "the American people can benefit from the success of AI," describing it as potentially "a beautiful thing."

The administration plans to meet with artificial intelligence companies in the coming week to discuss the equity-sharing arrangement. The concept has garnered interest across the political spectrum, with potential discussions involving major AI firms like OpenAI.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches mass drone attack on St. Petersburg naval base
cards.body:
Ukraine launched hundreds of drones targeting Russian military facilities in St. Petersburg on the final day of a major Russian investment forum in the city. The strikes focused on a naval base near the Russian city and represented the second long-range drone attack on St. Petersburg in recent days.

The attack came hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during the economic forum. Putin had been speaking at the event in St. Petersburg when Ukrainian forces executed the operation. The timing appeared designed to demonstrate Ukrainian strike capabilities deep inside Russian territory while Putin addressed international investors.

Multiple news outlets reported the strikes targeted Russian navy installations near St. Petersburg, a city located far from the Ukrainian border. The operation marked an escalation in Ukraine's use of long-range drone warfare against Russian military infrastructure. Ukraine has increasingly deployed drones to strike targets hundreds of miles inside Russia as the war continues.

The attack unfolded on what sources described as the last day of Putin's Davos-style investment forum in St. Petersburg. The forum had drawn international attention as Russia sought to project economic stability and attract foreign investment despite ongoing Western sanctions related to the war in Ukraine. The drone strikes overshadowed the event's final day and highlighted Ukraine's ability to reach Russian cities previously considered secure from attack.

Russian authorities have not released casualty figures or detailed damage assessments from the strikes. The attack represents part of a broader Ukrainian strategy to target Russian military facilities and disrupt operations far from the front lines. St. Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city and a major naval hub, has become an increasingly frequent target as Ukraine expands its drone program.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters should not receive pardons or compensation
cards.teaser: The former vice president said Friday that rioters who assaulted officers or vandalized property should never get a dime.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Friday that individuals who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property, or disrupted certification of the 2020 presidential election during the January 6 Capitol attack should not be pardoned by President Trump. He also stated such individuals should never receive financial compensation.

Pence made the remarks during an appearance on HBO's Real Time with Bill Maher, as the Trump administration considers how to handle cases related to the Capitol riot.

cards.headline: Armenian voters decide on pro-Western government under Russian pressure
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeks a third term as Moscow applies pressure on his administration.
cards.body:
Armenia held parliamentary elections as Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan sought a third term. His government has gradually shifted away from Russia toward closer Western ties, straining the traditionally close relationship between Moscow and Yerevan under Vladimir Putin.

Pashinyan faces domestic pressure from multiple directions: those wanting to maintain Russia ties and those frustrated with the pace of Western integration. The election outcome will shape Armenia's foreign policy direction going forward.

cards.headline: Israeli strike kills Lebanese general and two soldiers
cards.teaser: Three members of the Lebanese military died in an Israeli attack on a vehicle in south Lebanon.
cards.body:
A Lebanese general and two soldiers were killed in an Israeli strike on their vehicle in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military confirmed it hit the vehicle and said the incident is being reviewed.

Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the strike "a flagrant violation to Lebanese sovereignty and international law." The deaths mark a significant escalation involving the Lebanese armed forces, which have generally avoided direct conflict with Israel during recent fighting between Israeli forces and Hezbollah.

cards.headline: Neo-Nazi party member advances to mayoral runoff in eastern German town
cards.teaser: A candidate from a neo-Nazi party reached a mayoral runoff election in a small eastern German town, breaking with postwar voting patterns.
cards.body:
A member of a neo-Nazi party has advanced to a runoff election for mayor in a small town in eastern Germany. The development breaks with patterns established since the fall of the Third Reich, when German voters have consistently rejected mayoral candidates from neo-Nazi parties.

The runoff election is scheduled for Sunday in the eastern German town. The candidate's advancement to the final round reflects shifting political dynamics in parts of eastern Germany, where far-right parties have gained support in recent years. German voters will decide whether to elect the candidate or maintain the postwar tradition of blocking neo-Nazi politicians from local office.

cards.headline: Iran blocks technical staff from entering US for World Cup after players receive visas
cards.teaser: Iranian officials say technical staff were denied US visas hours after the State Department approved entry for players.
cards.body:
A diplomatic dispute has erupted over US visa approvals for Iran's World Cup delegation just days before the tournament begins. While the US state department approved visas for Iranian players and some coaching staff on June 5, several support staff members were reportedly denied entry, including Iranian football federation chief Mehdi Taj.

The visa denials threaten Iran's preparations as the team prepares to play all three group-stage matches in the United States, starting June 15 against New Zealand in Los Angeles. Iran's delegation trained and played closed-door matches in Turkey while diplomats worked to secure the necessary travel documents.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors announce election fraud probe in California
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorneys office in California opened an investigation into elections amid a slow ballot count and rising tensions.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as California's vote count continues at a slower-than-usual pace. The move comes as millions of ballots remain uncounted in races for governor, LA mayor, and Congress.

The delayed results have prompted unfounded claims of election irregularities. State officials have rejected allegations of impropriety in the primary elections.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers authorize strike ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Workers at the Los Angeles stadium voted to authorize a strike as negotiations continue with the hospitality group and FIFA.
cards.body:
Workers at SoFi Stadium voted to authorize a strike ahead of the World Cup. The authorization strengthens the union's position as negotiations continue with the hospitality group operating the Los Angeles venue and FIFA.

Talks between the parties are scheduled to resume on Monday. The strike vote gives the union increased leverage as it seeks agreements on working conditions and compensation for stadium workers.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as votes continue to be counted
cards.teaser: Raman closed in on Pratt as more votes were tallied in the Los Angeles mayoral race.
cards.body:
The gap between candidates Pratt and Raman narrowed in the fight for second place in the Los Angeles mayoral race as additional votes were counted. Raman closed in on Pratt as the tallying process continued.

Pratt's lead over Raman eroded further in new results released as voters await news on the California governors race. The ongoing count will determine which two candidates advance in the mayoral election.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes European migration policy in D-Day speech
cards.teaser: The U.S. defense secretary spoke in Normandy, 82 years after allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied Europe.
cards.body:
U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth delivered remarks in Normandy during D-Day commemorations marking 82 years since allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. He used the occasion to attack Europe's migration policies, drawing criticism for focusing on contemporary issues rather than the historical significance of the anniversary.

The speech drew attention for its unusual choice of subject matter at a solemn military commemoration event.

cards.headline: British Prime Minister Starmer says he will fight any leadership contest
cards.teaser: The prime minister's position hardened after Andy Burnham said he would seek to enter any potential Labour contest.
cards.body:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has told supporters he will contest any leadership challenge to his position. His resolve strengthened after Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, indicated he would enter a potential Labour party leadership race.

The statement clarifies Starmer's determination to remain party leader amid ongoing speculation about challenges to his authority. Burnham's declaration prompted the prime minister to publicly confirm his commitment to fighting for the role.

cards.headline: British lawmakers say delays to defense plan undermine UK credibility
cards.teaser: Members of Parliament criticized the postponement of the Defence Investment Plan, now due ahead of a NATO summit next month.
cards.body:
Members of Parliament said delays to the defense plan undermine UK credibility on the international stage. The Defence Investment Plan is now scheduled to be released ahead of a NATO summit early next month.

The postponement drew criticism from lawmakers who argued the delay weakens Britain's position within the alliance. The plan was expected earlier but has been pushed back to coincide with the upcoming summit.

hero.headline: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 in Worst Week Since FTX Collapse
hero.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 this week, marking the worst weekly performance for major cryptocurrencies since the November 2022 collapse of the FTX exchange. Ether also experienced sharp declines as digital assets erased all gains accumulated since the November 2024 presidential election.

The cryptocurrency fell to its lowest level since October 2024, wiping out months of price appreciation. Both Bitcoin and Ether suffered comparable percentage losses during the current downturn, reflecting broad weakness rather than isolated pressure on individual tokens.

The sell-off erased what had been a period of strength for cryptocurrencies following the 2024 election. Bitcoin had climbed steadily in the months after November, buoyed by expectations of favorable regulatory treatment and institutional adoption. Those gains have now been completely reversed, with prices falling below pre-election levels.

The magnitude of this week's decline places it among the most severe sell-offs in recent cryptocurrency history. The last comparable weekly decline occurred during the FTX crisis, when the major exchange's sudden bankruptcy triggered widespread panic selling across digital asset markets.

Market analysts pointed to several factors weighing on digital assets, though no single catalyst appeared to trigger the decline. The sharp reversal highlights ongoing volatility in cryptocurrency markets, where rapid price swings remain common despite growing institutional participation. Trading volumes increased during the sell-off as investors sought to exit positions, adding to downward pressure on prices.

The broader economic environment has also created headwinds for digital assets. Rising inflation and economic uncertainty stemming from geopolitical tensions have rattled financial markets more broadly. US stock markets experienced their own significant declines this week, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq index closing down 4 percent in a single day, the largest drop in over a year. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones also fell sharply.

Despite some recent positive economic indicators, including steady job growth in the labor market, investor sentiment remains fragile across asset classes. The combination of persistent inflation concerns and geopolitical risk has prompted investors to reassess their portfolios and reduce exposure to riskier investments, including cryptocurrencies.

This week's downturn demonstrates that cryptocurrency markets remain highly sensitive to broader economic shifts and investor sentiment. While institutional participation in digital assets has grown significantly over the past few years, the sector continues to experience sharp reversals that can wipe out substantial gains in relatively short timeframes. The speed at which Bitcoin erased nearly a year's worth of gains underscores the continued volatility that characterizes cryptocurrency investing, even as the market has matured considerably since the days of the FTX collapse.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Faces Market Capacity Questions at $1.8 Trillion Valuation
cards.teaser: Analysts question whether public markets can absorb a SpaceX offering at the company's reported valuation.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing to launch what would be the largest stock market debut in history, with shares set for release on June 12 at a $135 per-share valuation. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, raising $75 billion from the offering.

The IPO's unprecedented scale has drawn expert scrutiny about potential risks and market capacity. Notably, up to a quarter of the shares will be reserved for individual investors rather than institutional funds and banks—a significantly larger retail allocation than typical for major IPOs.

cards.headline: Pfizer Obesity Drug Shows Similar Side Effects to Wegovy in Trial
cards.teaser: Pfizer's monthly weight loss injection produced a side effect profile comparable to existing treatments in midstage testing.
cards.body:
Pfizer reported results from a midstage trial of its monthly obesity shot, showing side effects similar to Novo Nordisk's Wegovy. The pharmaceutical company is working to develop a weight loss treatment that requires less frequent dosing than current daily or weekly options on the market.

The company is betting on obesity drugs to drive growth over the next decade as demand for weight loss medications continues to expand. Pfizer's entry into the crowded GLP-1 obesity drug market comes as multiple pharmaceutical companies compete to develop next-generation treatments. The monthly dosing schedule represents an attempt to differentiate the product in a market where competitors are also developing less frequent injection options.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly Drug Shows Benefits for Sleep Apnea and Osteoarthritis in Obesity Patients
cards.teaser: Lilly's retatrutide reduced weight and improved multiple health conditions in clinical trials.
cards.body:
Eli Lilly shared safety and tolerability data for retatrutide, its next-generation obesity medication. The triple agonist drug demonstrated weight reduction along with improvements in A1C levels, knee osteoarthritis pain, and obstructive sleep apnea in patients with obesity.

The company positioned the drug as having potential to treat not just obesity but also related health complications. The results contribute to a wave of new weight loss therapies aimed at improving on current GLP-1 medications. Lilly presented the data as evidence of the drug's ability to address multiple conditions simultaneously in obesity patients.

cards.headline: Trump Considers Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The administration is exploring a plan for the U.S. government to take equity positions in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump is exploring the possibility of the U.S. government acquiring equity stakes in AI companies. Trump framed the proposal as a way for "the American people can benefit from the success of AI," describing it as potentially "a beautiful thing."

The administration plans to meet with artificial intelligence companies in the coming week to discuss the equity-sharing arrangement. The concept has garnered interest across the political spectrum, with potential discussions involving major AI firms like OpenAI.

cards.headline: Bank of America Adjusts Broadcom Price Target After Earnings
cards.teaser: The bank reset its stock price target for the chipmaker following quarterly results.
cards.body:
Bank of America adjusted its price target for Broadcom shares after the company reported earnings. The semiconductor company's stock has declined following the results, which some analysts characterized as an overreaction to conservative guidance provided by management.

Investment analysts remain divided on Broadcom's outlook, with some seeing significant upside potential while others point to continued pressure on the stock. The chipmaker's earnings prompted reassessments across Wall Street as investors evaluate the company's growth trajectory and valuation.

cards.headline: Major Corporations Fund Training Programs to Address Skilled Labor Shortage
cards.teaser: Large companies are spending to create pipelines for mechanics and electricians as demand outpaces supply.
cards.body:
Big businesses are investing in training programs to develop mechanics, electricians, and other skilled tradespeople as the U.S. faces shortages in these occupations. The corporate spending reflects growing concern about workforce gaps that threaten operations and growth.

The collision repair industry's technician pipeline currently fills only 42 percent of demand, according to a TechForce report. Multiple industries report similar shortfalls in skilled workers, prompting companies to take direct action rather than relying solely on traditional vocational education systems. The programs aim to create sustainable talent pipelines for positions that require specialized technical skills.

hero.headline: OpenAI launches Lockdown Mode to defend against prompt injection attacks
hero.body:
OpenAI Delays Adult Mode as Company Prioritizes AI Safety and Performance

OpenAI has postponed the launch of its planned "adult mode" for ChatGPT, shifting focus to what the company considers more urgent priorities. Chief Executive Sam Altman had previously announced that OpenAI would permit adult content once it implemented age verification systems. The company now says this timeline has been extended.

"We're pushing out the launch of adult mode so we can focus on work that is a higher priority for more users right now, including gains in intelligence, personality improvements, personalisation, and making the experience more proactive," OpenAI stated. The company serves over 900 million ChatGPT users globally.

Since announcing the adult mode plan last October, Altman has declared a "code red" initiative to enhance ChatGPT's capabilities amid intense competition from rivals including Google and Anthropic. The delay reflects this strategic shift toward improving core functionality rather than expanding content policies.

While the adult mode rollout waits, OpenAI is deploying age prediction tools that identify users under 18. Young users automatically receive enhanced safety settings that limit exposure to graphic violence and sexual role-play content. In the United Kingdom, OpenAI must comply with the Online Safety Act by using strict age verification to shield pornographic images from minors.

OpenAI continues to stand by its foundational principle of respecting adult autonomy. "We still believe in the principle of treating adults like adults, but getting the experience right will take more time," the company said.

The delay announcement comes amid broader scrutiny of OpenAI's operational practices. A senior manager recently resigned over the company's Department of Defense partnership, raising governance concerns. Caitlin Kalinowski, head of hardware within OpenAI's robotics division, stepped down citing worries about mass surveillance of American citizens and AI-guided autonomous weapons.

Kalinowski stated that while she respected leadership, the Pentagon deal's rapid execution troubled her. "To be clear, my issue is that the announcement was rushed without the guardrails defined. It's a governance concern first and foremost. These are too important for deals or announcements to be rushed," she wrote on social media.

OpenAI acknowledged the Pentagon contract needed refinement. The company has amended its agreement to explicitly exclude domestic surveillance applications and autonomous weapons use. An OpenAI spokesperson explained that the revised contract "creates a workable path for responsible national security uses of AI while making clear our red lines: no domestic surveillance and no autonomous weapons."

The company acknowledged that "people have strong views about these issues" and committed to ongoing dialogue with employees, government officials, civil society groups, and international communities regarding these sensitive matters.

cards.headline: Sriram Krishnan leaves White House AI advisor role
cards.teaser: Krishnan is reportedly launching a new institution to continue influencing Trump administration AI policy from outside government.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan departed his position as AI advisor in the White House, ending his tenure shaping artificial intelligence policy within the Trump administration. The technology executive had been serving in the role as the federal government worked to establish regulatory frameworks for AI development and deployment.

Krishnan plans to start a new institution focused on AI policy, where he will reportedly continue working to influence the Trump administration's approach to artificial intelligence. The move suggests he will maintain involvement in government AI strategy from an external position rather than as a federal employee.

cards.headline: Scientists discover world's largest scorpion species from 415 million years ago
cards.teaser: Fossils reveal ancient scorpions grew over three feet long with six-inch pincers during the Devonian Period in Britain.
cards.body:
Scientists identified the largest scorpion species ever to exist based on 415-million-year-old fossils discovered in Britain. The creatures grew to over three feet in length and possessed pincers measuring six inches, making them comparable in size to baseball bats. The scorpions lived during the Devonian Period and inhabited both land and water environments.

The Natural History Museum and other research institutions analyzed the fossils to determine the dimensions and characteristics of these ancient arthropods. The discovery provides new insight into the scale of prehistoric life forms that existed hundreds of millions of years before dinosaurs. The massive scorpions represent some of the largest arthropods to have lived on Earth.

cards.headline: Chemists demonstrate how RNA may have replicated itself on early Earth
cards.teaser: Researchers solved a decades-old problem in origin-of-life science by showing how RNA could have copied itself without modern cellular machinery.
cards.body:
Chemists demonstrated for the first time a plausible mechanism by which RNA molecules could have replicated themselves on early Earth. The breakthrough addresses a fundamental question that has stalled origin-of-life research for decades: how genetic material copied itself before the existence of the complex cellular machinery that performs this task in modern organisms.

The research represents a significant advance in understanding how life may have emerged from non-living chemistry. RNA is believed to have played a central role in early life because it can both store genetic information and catalyze chemical reactions. The new findings show how this self-replication could have occurred under conditions thought to exist on the primitive Earth billions of years ago.

cards.headline: Apple's WWDC 2026 to feature Siri overhaul and Apple Intelligence updates
cards.teaser: The company's annual developer conference will showcase a major revision to its voice assistant alongside enhancements to its AI platform.
cards.body:
Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference will include a substantial redesign of Siri, the company's voice assistant that has faced criticism for lagging behind competitors. The event will also feature updates to Apple Intelligence, the company's artificial intelligence platform introduced in previous product releases.

The conference represents Apple's latest effort to demonstrate progress in AI capabilities as the technology industry focuses heavily on generative AI and language models. Developers and consumers have anticipated improvements to Siri's functionality and accuracy, areas where the assistant has been perceived as weaker than rival products from Google and Amazon.

cards.headline: New telescope facility to begin decade-long survey of unseen solar system objects
cards.teaser: Millions of objects within our solar system have never been observed, and a new facility will start cataloging them in the coming months.
cards.body:
A new astronomical facility will begin a decade-long survey within months to identify and track millions of objects in the solar system that have never been observed. The project aims to catalog asteroids, comets, and other bodies that remain undetected despite existing within Earth's cosmic neighborhood.

The survey will provide scientists with a comprehensive map of the solar system's contents, improving understanding of its composition and history. The facility's capabilities will allow detection of objects that are too small, distant, or dim to have been spotted by previous telescopes. The data collected will also help assess potential collision risks from near-Earth objects.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors studio announces Switch 2 version and expansion plans
cards.teaser: The indie game will launch on Nintendo's next console while developer poncle establishes a Japan studio and releases new downloadable content.
cards.body:
Vampire Survivors is coming to Nintendo Switch 2, developer poncle confirmed. The indie hit will be adapted for the upcoming console hardware as part of the studio's growth strategy.

Poncle is establishing a new studio in Japan under the leadership of Sawaki Takeyasu, creator of El Shaddai. The studio is also developing an "evil twin" DLC expansion for Vampire Survivors alongside these announcements.

hero.headline: Mitch Marner scores Stanley Cup Final hat trick as Vegas outlasts Carolina in double overtime
hero.body:
Vegas Holds Off Carolina's Comeback to Take 2-1 Series Lead

Shea Theodore scored at 5:38 of the second overtime period to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 5-4 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final on Saturday night. The goal, which deflected off goalie Brandon Bussi's skate, secured a 2-1 series lead for Vegas after the Hurricanes mounted a dramatic fourth-period rally.

The Golden Knights appeared to be cruising to victory thanks to a dominant second period from Mitch Marner, who recorded the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history. Marner's three goals gave Vegas a commanding four-goal advantage heading into the final period, seemingly putting the game out of reach.

Carolina had other ideas. The Hurricanes stormed back in the third period, scoring four consecutive goals to erase Vegas's lead and force the game into overtime. The comeback shifted momentum entirely, transforming what looked like a comfortable Golden Knights victory into one of the most dramatic playoff contests in recent memory.

Both teams created chances during the first overtime period but failed to convert. The game remained deadlocked until Theodore's heroic finish in the second overtime, ending one of the most unpredictable Stanley Cup Final games in recent years.

Theodore's winning goal prevented what could have been a devastating collapse for Vegas. The Golden Knights had been in complete control for much of the game, with Marner's historic performance appearing to have settled the outcome. Instead, the Hurricanes proved their resilience and staying power, nearly completing an improbable comeback before Theodore's late heroics.

The victory gave Vegas the advantage in the series as the two teams prepared to continue their Finals matchup. The combination of Marner's record-setting achievement and Carolina's furious comeback created a contest that showcased the intensity and unpredictability characteristic of championship-level hockey. The game took place in front of a capacity crowd that witnessed playoff hockey at its most dramatic.

Marner's hat trick stands as a milestone in Stanley Cup Final history. His three goals in the second period represented the fastest such performance in the Finals' long history, cementing his place in the record books regardless of the game's ultimate outcome.

The Hurricanes' ability to score four consecutive goals demonstrated their determination and offensive capability, even as they fell short in the end. The loss was particularly difficult given how close they came to completing an extraordinary comeback and potentially shifting the series momentum entirely in their favor.

With the series now favoring Vegas 2-1, both teams faced the prospect of continuing their battle for the Stanley Cup. The dramatic nature of Game 3 promised that subsequent games would be contested with similar intensity and urgency.

cards.headline: Gabriel Bonfim dominates Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas
cards.teaser: Gabriel Bonfim delivered a dominant performance against Belal Muhammad in the main event of UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
The fight took place at UFC Vegas 118, with Bonfim controlling the bout against the experienced Muhammad. Following the victory, Bonfim called out Jack Della Maddalena as a potential next opponent, signaling his intentions to continue climbing the welterweight rankings.

The event also featured preliminary card action, with multiple matchups drawing attention from MMA analysts. The Las Vegas card marked another installment in the UFC's ongoing Fight Night series, which regularly features rising contenders and established veterans competing outside of pay-per-view events.

cards.headline: Bryce Mitchell secures dramatic last-second submission at UFC Vegas 118
cards.teaser: Bryce Mitchell pulled off a dramatic submission victory in the final seconds of his bout with Santiago Luna at UFC Fight Night 278.
cards.body:
Mitchell pulled off a stunning submission victory in the final seconds of his UFC Vegas 118 bout, securing a dramatic finish that prevented a decision loss. The submission showcased his resilience after a challenging fight against Luna, who had stepped in on short notice.

The win proved significant for Mitchell's trajectory in the organization, coming during a period that had generated considerable discussion about his future in the UFC.

cards.headline: Golden Tempo wins Belmont Stakes at Saratoga one month after Kentucky Derby victory
cards.teaser: Golden Tempo captured the Belmont Stakes at Saratoga Race Course, adding to the horse's Kentucky Derby triumph from one month earlier.
cards.body:
Golden Tempo captured the 158th Belmont Stakes on Saturday at Saratoga Race Course, with jockey Jose Ortiz guiding the horse to victory five weeks after winning the Kentucky Derby. Golden Tempo crossed the finish line ahead of Commandment, winning at 6-1 odds.

The victory adds another chapter to trainer Cherie DeVaux's historic year. DeVaux becomes the latest trainer to win both the Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes in the same season, cementing her place among racing's elite. Renegade, the race favorite, finished third.

cards.headline: North Carolina forces Game 3 against USC with 4-0 win in Super Regional
cards.teaser: The North Carolina baseball team shut out USC 4-0 to even their Super Regional series and force a decisive third game.
cards.body:
Jason DeCaro threw a complete-game shutout for the Tar Heels, keeping North Carolina's season alive after facing elimination. The performance came after USC had taken the first game of the series behind a grand slam from Braden Carpentier that appeared to shift momentum in the Trojans' favor.

The Super Regional series will now be decided in a winner-take-all Game 3. North Carolina entered the contest needing a victory to avoid the end of their season, and DeCaro delivered what analysts described as a gem on the mound to keep the Diamond Heels' College World Series hopes intact.

cards.headline: Chase Elliott earns pole position for NASCAR Cup race at Michigan
cards.teaser: Chase Elliott will lead Hendrick Motorsports to the green flag after winning the pole for the NASCAR Cup Series race at Michigan.
cards.body:
Elliott topped qualifying at Michigan International Speedway, giving Hendrick Motorsports the front-row starting position. The high-speed track presents unique challenges, with Toyota having shown historical dominance at the venue in recent years.

The race features questions about whether Chevrolet and Ford teams can challenge Toyota's strong performance record at Michigan. Elliott's pole position gives Hendrick a strategic advantage heading into a race where speeds and stakes are both elevated.

cards.headline: Michael van Gerwen rallies to beat Luke Humphries in Nordic Darts Masters final
cards.teaser: Michael van Gerwen came from behind to defeat Luke Humphries 8-7 in the final leg of the Nordic Darts Masters in Denmark.
cards.body:
Michael van Gerwen claimed the Nordic Darts Masters title in Denmark with a dramatic 8-7 victory over Luke Humphries. Van Gerwen came from behind to win the final leg and secure the championship.

The comeback proved decisive as Humphries had led for much of the match before van Gerwen's late surge turned the result around.

hero.headline: Kennedy Center Loses Lawsuit Against Musician Who Canceled Concert After Trump Naming Dispute
hero.body:
A judge has dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Kennedy Center against jazz drummer and vibes player Chuck Redd, who withdrew from a Christmas Eve performance after the venue announced plans to add Donald Trump's name to the facility.

Redd had been scheduled to perform at the Kennedy Center's annual free "Christmas Eve Jazz Jam" but canceled after the White House announced the naming change. The Kennedy Center subsequently sued the musician, seeking $1 million in damages for the breach of contract.

In her ruling, DC Superior Court Judge Tanya Jones Bosier found that Kennedy Center officials had failed to establish a legally binding agreement with Redd. "I could not find a valid breach-of-contract claim here," Bosier said. "There's no dispute that he did not sign the 2025 agreement."

The judge granted Redd's motion to dismiss under the District of Columbia's anti-Slapp law, which prevents lawsuits intended to silence opposing views on matters of public interest. This legal protection is specifically designed to protect free speech rights.

Richard Grenell, then the Kennedy Center's president, had threatened legal action shortly after Redd canceled. Grenell stated the center would pursue damages for what he called "this political stunt," accusing Redd of intolerance. The center filed suit in March and initially offered to settle if Redd paid $7,500, performed at this year's concert, and refrained from making "political commentary" about his withdrawal.

Lisa J Banks, one of Redd's lawyers, said in a statement that the lawsuit constituted political retaliation. "The Center sued Mr Redd because he publicly and rightly objected to adding Donald Trump's name to the Kennedy Center, a living memorial to former President John F Kennedy," Banks said. "The lawsuit against Mr Redd was political retribution, pure and simple, by the Trump Kennedy Center, and the Court correctly saw it as such in dismissing the case with prejudice."

Redd told the Associated Press he was "very pleased" by the ruling.

The dismissal comes after another judge previously ordered the removal of Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade and website. That ruling determined that the performing arts venue, which Congress designated as a living memorial to former President John F Kennedy, cannot be renamed without an act of Congress.

The case drew significant attention from the arts community as cultural institutions navigate political controversies and performers grapple with questions about artistic freedom and contractual obligations. The dismissal allows Redd to proceed without facing financial penalties or other legal consequences related to his decision to withdraw from the performance. The Kennedy Center has not indicated whether it plans to appeal the ruling.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Debuts Duet With The Cure's Robert Smith at Primavera Sound Festival
cards.teaser: The pop star premiered a new song featuring the legendary rock vocalist during a surprise performance in Spain.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo brought Robert Smith of The Cure onstage during a surprise set at the Primavera Sound festival to debut their collaboration titled What's Wrong With Me. The duet appears on Rodrigo's forthcoming album, which is scheduled for release within the week. The collaboration had been kept secret until the live premiere.

Rodrigo performed the surprise set at the Spanish music festival, revealing one of what she described as the best-kept secrets of 2026. The pairing brings together one of pop's biggest current stars with the frontman of the influential rock band The Cure. Smith joined Rodrigo partway through her performance to unveil the new track.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Marry in Sicily Ceremony
cards.teaser: The pop star and actor held a wedding celebration in Italy that included a performance by Elton John.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner married in Sicily in a ceremony that featured Elton John serenading the couple with Your Song. The wedding took place in Palermo, where the bride wore a leather outfit as part of her wedding attire. Multiple sources confirmed the marriage took place in Italy.

The Palermo ceremony drew mixed reactions locally, with some residents questioning the attention given to the celebrity wedding. The event brought together guests and performers for the couple's Italian celebration. John's performance of his classic ballad served as a highlight of the wedding festivities.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Thanks Supporters After 60 Minutes Firing
cards.teaser: The veteran correspondent addressed fans on social media following his termination by the show's new executive producer.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley posted a message on Instagram thanking supporters after being fired from 60 Minutes by the program's new executive producer, Nick Bilton. Pelley wrote that his fans are the wind in my sails and expressed gratitude for the kind messages he received.

In a follow-up statement, Pelley accused CBS News executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into his reporting. He claimed the network's new management silenced employees while compromising journalistic integrity. Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes built its decades-long success on integrity and quality storytelling.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Cancels Second Pittsburgh Concert Due to Severe Weather
cards.teaser: The country star called off his Acrisure Stadium show amid threats of inclement weather.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled his second scheduled concert at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh due to severe weather threats. The country music star decided to cancel rather than risk performing in dangerous conditions.

A local baseball team responded to the cancellation by offering affected concertgoers free admission to their games, providing an alternative for disappointed fans.

cards.headline: Charlie Puth Cancels Orlando Concert Due to Illness
cards.teaser: The pop singer announced he was instructed to rest after being sick for several days.
cards.body:
Charlie Puth canceled his Saturday concert in Orlando, Florida, after falling ill. The singer announced the cancellation on his Instagram Story, expressing his devastation about the decision. He explained that he had been sick for several days and needed to rest on medical advice.

Puth prioritized his health over the performance, acknowledging the disappointment for fans who had planned to attend the show.

cards.headline: John C. Reilly Says He Urged Leonardo DiCaprio to Turn Down Titanic
cards.teaser: The actor recounted trying to convince DiCaprio to star in Boogie Nights instead of the James Cameron blockbuster.
cards.body:
John C. Reilly recently shared on the "Where Everybody Knows Your Name" podcast that he tried to persuade Leonardo DiCaprio to reject Titanic in favor of Boogie Nights. Close with director Paul Thomas Anderson after their collaboration, Reilly attempted to steer DiCaprio toward Anderson's film instead.

DiCaprio ultimately chose Titanic, which became one of the highest-grossing films ever made. Boogie Nights proceeded with a different cast, and the anecdote offers a glimpse into the career decisions DiCaprio faced during a pivotal moment in Hollywood.

hero.headline: President Trump to appear on Meet the Press as midterm pressures mount
hero.teaser: Trump faces an interview Sunday following a week marked by low approval ratings and public tensions with Senate Republicans.
hero.body:
President Trump will sit down for an interview Sunday on NBC's Meet the Press after a turbulent week that saw new lows in his approval ratings and growing tensions with Senate Republicans. The conflicts with members of his own party have increasingly spilled into public view.

The interview comes as midterm elections approach and the president faces mounting political pressure on key issues including the economy. Trump's relationship with Senate Republicans has become strained as lawmakers navigate their own electoral concerns while managing their ties to the White House.

The timing of the appearance reflects broader challenges facing the administration. As the midterm campaign intensifies, the president is working to address concerns among party members about the direction of his presidency and its impact on their own electoral prospects.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration has announced several initiatives aimed at reshaping American institutions and policy. The treasury department revealed that Trump's signature will appear on US paper currency, marking the first time a sitting president's name has been featured on legal tender. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the move aligns with efforts to promote economic growth and dollar strength. The first new currency bearing Trump's signature and Bessent's will be printed in June, with additional denominations following in subsequent months.

The administration has also pursued commemorative coins featuring Trump's image. The federal arts commission approved designs for 24-carat gold coins bearing the president's likeness, a decision that comes despite federal law restricting living presidents from appearing on currency.

These efforts represent an expansion of Trump's efforts to place his name and likeness on American institutions. The administration has renamed the US Institute of Peace, the Kennedy Center performing arts venue, and commissioned a new class of battleships, among other changes.

On the international front, the administration faces challenges abroad. Tensions with Iran have escalated following a series of military exchanges between the countries, threatening the fragile ceasefire in place. The United Nations has warned that the ongoing Middle East conflict is pushing millions into hunger, with oil price increases devastating global food security. The World Food Programme director noted that negative predictions about the humanitarian situation are materializing nearly three months into the conflict.

Trade policy remains another significant challenge. The administration's approach to tariffs and trade disputes continues to generate friction with international partners and concerns about the direction of US economic policy. Analysts warn that the scattershot approach to tariffs and trade negotiations could lead to a prolonged trade war with significant global implications.

As Trump prepares for his Sunday television appearance, these interconnected pressures from within his party, economic concerns, and international challenges will likely feature prominently in the discussion.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office has opened an investigation into alleged election fraud in California's primary elections.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced an investigation into election fraud in California's elections as the state continues counting votes from its primary election.

The probe announcement follows criticism from conservative figures, including President Trump and former Speaker Kevin McCarthy, who have challenged California's vote-counting process. McCarthy expressed concerns on Friday that California voters were losing confidence as results continued to arrive from the primary election.

cards.headline: White House AI policy adviser Sriram Krishnan to step down at end of June
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this mo.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a senior White House policy adviser on artificial intelligence, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of June. The tech investor has been instrumental in shaping the Trump administration's approach to AI policy and strategy.

Krishnan's departure removes a key voice from the administration's technology policy team during an active period for AI regulation and development debates in Congress. The White House has not yet announced who will replace him or how his responsibilities will be handled going forward.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters should not receive pardons or compensation
cards.teaser: The former vice president said Friday that rioters who assaulted officers or vandalized property should never get a dime.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Friday that individuals who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property, or disrupted certification of the 2020 presidential election during the January 6 Capitol attack should not be pardoned by President Trump. He also stated such individuals should never receive financial compensation.

Pence made the remarks during an appearance on HBO's Real Time with Bill Maher, as the Trump administration considers how to handle cases related to the Capitol riot.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary under President Biden, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Sunday. Her victory sets up a general election race in November where she could make history.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She previously served as a U.S. representative from New Mexico before joining the Biden administration, where she was the first Native American Cabinet secretary.

cards.headline: Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra lead in California governor primary as counting continues
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are ahead as results continue to come in to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's gubernatorial primary as vote counting continues. Becerra has advanced to the general election after a remarkable turnaround—his polling stood near 3% in late March before surging in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

If elected in November, Becerra would make history as California's first Latino governor since 1875, when Romualdo Pacheco briefly served as governor during the territorial period. The extended counting process reflects California's mail-in ballot system, which allows ballots postmarked by election day to be counted if they arrive within days of the election.

cards.headline: NYC Mayor Mamdani says Democrats have lost focus on working-class Americans
cards.teaser: The Democratic mayor said Saturday the party has shifted away from economic issues facing working people.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Saturday that the Democratic Party has lost sight of important economic issues facing working-class Americans. He made the comments as the party works to rebuild itself following its loss in the 2024 presidential election.

Mamdani told interviewers that the party as a whole has lost its focus on working people. His critique adds to ongoing internal discussions within the Democratic Party about how to reconnect with voters who feel the party has moved away from their economic concerns.
